grammar_choice.en_template: Some people are more likely {{1:to cheat/cheating}} and steal after {{2:purchasing/purchase}} "eco-friendly" products, probably because they feel licensed to do so.

grammar_choice.en_template: Moral licensing has also {{1:been/being}} observed in the {{2:context/contexts}} of cooperation for the good of the environment.

grammar_choice.en_template: When people are {{1:reminded/reminding}} of deeds they have done that they know {{2:were/being}} harmful to the environment, they might be left with a feeling of "eco-guilt."

explain: 사람들이 '상기되는' 대상 → 수동태 are reminded of.
관계절의 정동사가 필요 → were (they know는 삽입절).

grammar_choice.en_template: People who {{1:experience/experiences}} eco-guilt seek pro-environmental actions to compensate for this guilt and {{2:restore/restoring}} balance.

grammar_choice.en_template: In their search for such a balance, people are eager to believe in "quick-fixes," {{1:because/because of}} they want to escape the guilt as quickly and {{2:easily/easy}} as possible.

explain: 뒤에 절(they want ~)이 오므로 접속사 because.

fill_first_letter.ko_full: 도덕적 면허 효과는 환경을 위한 협력의 맥락에서도 관찰되어 왔다.
사람들이 환경에 해로웠다고 스스로 알고 있는 자신의 행동들을 상기하게 되면, "환경적 죄책감"이라는 감정이 남을 수 있다.
환경적 죄책감을 경험하는 사람들은 이 죄책감을 보상하고 균형을 회복하기 위해 친환경적 행동을 찾는다.
그러한 균형을 찾는 과정에서 사람들은 "손쉬운 해결책"을 믿기를 꺼리는데, 도덕적 균형을 되찾고 가능한 한 빠르고 쉽게 죄책감에서 벗어나고 싶어 하기 때문이다.
사람들이 태도와 행동 사이의 불일치를 줄이려 태도를 바꿀 수 있는 것과 마찬가지로, 과거의 환경 부담 행동과 미래의 친환경 행동에 대한 평가도 바꿀 수 있다.
예를 들어, 사람들은 인간이 초래한 환경 훼손의 증거를 본 뒤에 환경 훼손을 다루는 청원서에 서명할 가능성이 더 높다.

jumble.answer: Some people are more likely to cheat and steal after purchasing "eco-friendly" products, probably because they feel licensed to do so.
Moral licensing has also been observed in the context of cooperation for the good of the environment.
When people are reminded of deeds they have done that they know were harmful to the environment, they might be left with a feeling of "eco-guilt."
People who experience eco-guilt seek pro-environmental actions to compensate for this guilt and restore balance.
In their search for such a balance, people are reluctant to believe in "quick-fixes," because they want to escape the guilt as quickly and easily as possible.
In the same way that people may change their attitudes to reduce inconsistencies between attitudes and behavior, people may also change their evaluation of past behaviors.
For instance, people are more likely to sign a petition addressing environmental damage after viewing evidence of human-caused environmental damage.
